cells.tense: The strength is moving outward now, and the measure is yours to keep.
cells.ask: Offer one concrete piece of help today, name it out loud, and let it land without watching for it to come back.
cells.core:
Most of what you carry reaches other people in small, deliberate amounts. You notice what's running low somewhere and you put something there, and you don't make a story about it. That's strength moving outward by measure, and it holds because you're not spending past what you have.

The clearing around you didn't cost you your footing. Something that wasn't holding fell away recently, and instead of pulling back you kept letting what you have flow toward where it's wanted. The one thing to keep an eye on is the size of the pour. This works when you pick the amount on purpose, the way you have been, and the ask today is one piece of help offered plainly — nothing more than you'd choose to give twice.
cells.sheetLine: You share by measure, and the measure is still yours.
cells.place: in the middle of a clearing, where something that couldn't hold is coming down

cells.tense: You're bracing for the next clearing and handing out strength before it's asked for.
cells.ask: Before your next offer of help, check one thing: whether that person owes it to you, or you to them — then act on what you find.
cells.core:
You're already picturing the collapse that hasn't happened — the thing that's going to come apart, the people who'll need catching — and you're handing out strength ahead of the hand reaching for it. The pace has picked up. Every need you spot feels like yours to meet before it turns into a problem, so nothing gets the chance to arrive on its own.

That's strength pushing at a future it can't write. You can carry a lot, that's the point of you, and carrying without forcing is the other side of the same thing. What matters isn't the size of the load. It's whether what you're handing over is actually owed, and owing runs both directions. Check the ledger with one person before you open your hands again.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying loads nobody has handed you yet.

cells.tense: You gave everything you had, and you're still standing at the door you already walked through.
cells.ask: Let one person hand you something small this week, accept it the first time it's offered, and don't try to hand it back.
cells.core:
The old structure fell, and you were the one holding part of it up while it went. Something got spent in that, and the strength you used to share isn't moving outward anymore; it isn't coming back in either. You talk about it the way you'd talk about a week that's already behind you.

What's gone quiet isn't your ability to hold. It's your part in it. Being the one who gives is a place to stand, and going back to it isn't the first move. The first move is letting something land on you, from a hand that's offering it plainly. Finishing and surrender aren't the same thing here. If you take one small thing from one person this week, the clearing doesn't need to be relived — it's just room you're already standing in.
cells.sheetLine: You gave it all out, and you've stopped letting anything land.

cells.tense: You're already the support in this room, and you keep talking about it as circumstance.
cells.ask: Say one true sentence out loud to someone: 'I'm the one keeping this going' — about a task you've been calling how it works.
cells.core:
Look at what's actually running in the room. You're the one who notices first, who remembers what's needed, who covers the gap before anyone names it. That's strength moving outward, and it's been moving for a while. Somewhere in the telling, though, it became something that happens around you rather than something you do.

The clearing is room enough. What's missing is your own name on it. The version of you who gives like this picked it at some point, and that choosing is still yours to speak. Pick one task you carry, put your name on it, and tell one person in plain words that it was you.
cells.sheetLine: You keep this going. You've been calling it the situation.

attempts.check: The draft's weakest claim is that the person's support clearly caused or will cause a breakthrough; the record only seats the card in that place, it does not say the collapse of the false structure is already underway in their life. A reader could fairly say the clearing hasn't happened, and I've been describing a room they're not in yet. The asks survive that objection because each is one plain act — one load lifted, one account checked, one small help accepted, one hour named — useful whether or not my read of the moment is right. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any tidy 'the structure is already falling,' so I've left it out.
